title: FlytWERX ACS Maneuver Standards Checker Data

acs.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

page.disclaimer: This checker summarizes selected FAA ACS performance standards for training and debrief use. Always use the current official FAA ACS and the applicable POH/AFM. FlytWERX data supports review and does not replace evaluator judgment or approved aircraft indications.

normal-takeoff.name: Normal Takeoff

metrics.label: Climb Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the manufacturer-recommended climb speed or VY.

metrics.label: VY to Safe Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain VY to a safe maneuvering altitude.

metrics.label: Directional Control
metrics.description: Maintain directional control and wind-drift correction.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Use manufacturer-recommended configuration and procedures.

criteria: Complete appropriate checklist, runway verification, traffic scan, and radio calls.
Position controls for existing wind and align with runway centerline.
Apply takeoff power smoothly and verify proper indications.
Rotate at the recommended airspeed and establish the recommended climb speed or VY within ±5 knots.
Maintain directional control and wind correction during climb.
Maintain VY within ±5 knots to a safe maneuvering altitude.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

crosswind-takeoff.name: Crosswind Takeoff
crosswind-takeoff.displayNote: The Commercial Pilot ACS does not create a separate crosswind-takeoff task; wind correction and directional control are evaluated within the applicable takeoff task.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

soft-field-takeoff.name: Soft-Field Takeoff

metrics.label: VX / VY
metrics.description: Establish and maintain VX or VY as appropriate.

metrics.label: Ground Effect
metrics.description: Lift off at the lowest practical airspeed and remain in ground effect while accelerating.

metrics.label: VY to Safe Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain VY to a safe maneuvering altitude.

criteria: Use appropriate soft-field control positioning and minimize wheel loading.
Apply takeoff power smoothly while maintaining directional control.
Lift off at the lowest practical airspeed and remain in ground effect while accelerating.
Establish VX or VY as appropriate and maintain it within ±5 knots.
Retract gear/flaps in accordance with POH/AFM and a positive rate of climb.
Maintain VY within ±5 knots to a safe maneuvering altitude.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND ROLL
reviewVariables.text: Review wheel-loading reduction and directional control.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND EFFECT
reviewVariables.text: Review acceleration while remaining in ground effect.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

short-field-takeoff.name: Short-Field Takeoff

metrics.label: Obstacle / VX
metrics.description: Maintain recommended obstacle-clearance airspeed or VX.

metrics.label: VY
metrics.description: Accelerate to and maintain VY after obstacle clearance or 50 feet AGL when simulated.

metrics.label: Takeoff Area
metrics.description: Use the maximum available takeoff area.

metrics.label: Obstacle Transition
metrics.description: Transition after obstacle clearance or 50 feet AGL when simulated.

criteria: Use the maximum available takeoff area and appropriate short-field configuration.
Set takeoff power and verify proper indications.
Rotate at the recommended airspeed.
Establish and maintain obstacle-clearance airspeed or VX within ±5 knots.
After obstacle clearance or 50 feet AGL when simulated, accelerate to VY within ±5 knots.
Maintain VY within ±5 knots to a safe maneuvering altitude.

reviewVariables.label: RUNWAY USE
reviewVariables.text: Review use of available takeoff distance.

reviewVariables.label: TRANSITION
reviewVariables.text: Review transition from VX to VY.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards
source.taskName: Short-Field Takeoff and Maximum Performance Climb (ASEL, AMEL)

normal-landing.name: Normal Landing

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain published approach airspeed or ACS fallback with gust factor as applicable.

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 200 feet beyond the specified point.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift.

metrics.label: Alignment
metrics.description: Maintain runway alignment and directional control.

criteria: Complete checklist, runway verification, traffic scan, and radio calls.
Establish the recommended configuration and a stabilized approach.
Maintain published approach airspeed within ±5 knots with gust factor as applicable.
Maintain directional control and appropriate crosswind correction.
Touch down within 200 feet beyond or on the specified point with no side drift.
Execute a timely go-around if the approach cannot be completed within tolerance or safely.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Review touchdown location against the 200-foot window.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

crosswind-landing.name: Crosswind Landing
crosswind-landing.displayNote: The Commercial Pilot ACS does not create a separate crosswind-landing task; crosswind correction is evaluated within the applicable landing task.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

soft-field-landing.name: Soft-Field Landing

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain published approach airspeed or ACS fallback with gust factor as applicable.

metrics.label: Sink Rate
metrics.description: Touch down at minimum practical sink rate with proper pitch attitude.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift.

criteria: Establish a stabilized soft-field approach with appropriate configuration.
Maintain published approach airspeed within ±5 knots with gust factor as applicable.
Maintain directional control and crosswind correction.
Touch down softly at a proper pitch attitude with minimum sink rate and no side drift.
Maintain appropriate elevator/control position to minimize wheel loading during rollout.
Execute a go-around if the approach becomes unsafe or unstable.

reviewVariables.label: ROLLOUT
reviewVariables.text: Review wheel loading and directional control.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

short-field-landing.name: Short-Field Landing

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain published approach airspeed or ACS fallback with gust factor as applicable.

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 100 feet beyond the specified point, threshold markings, or runway numbers.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift and proper alignment.

metrics.label: Braking
metrics.description: Use appropriate braking and aerodynamic control consistent with POH/AFM.

criteria: Establish a stabilized short-field approach using appropriate configuration.
Maintain published approach airspeed within ±5 knots with gust factor as applicable.
Maintain directional control and crosswind correction.
Touch down within 100 feet beyond or on the specified point with minimum float and no side drift.
Use appropriate braking and control inputs after touchdown.
Execute a timely go-around if the approach cannot be completed within tolerance or safely.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Review touchdown location against the 100-foot window.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

power-off-180-landing.name: Power-Off 180° Accuracy Landing

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 200 feet beyond the specified point.

metrics.label: Power
metrics.description: Complete the maneuver power-off after the designated point.

metrics.label: Energy
metrics.description: Use pitch, configuration, and ground track to manage energy to the selected point.

criteria: Position the airplane appropriately for a power-off 180-degree accuracy approach.
Close the throttle at the designated point and establish the appropriate glide.
Plan the ground track and use configuration changes to manage energy.
Maintain coordinated flight and appropriate wind correction.
Touch down at a proper pitch attitude within 200 feet beyond or on the specified point with no side drift.
Maintain directional control through rollout.

reviewVariables.label: GLIDE
reviewVariables.text: Review glidepath and energy state after power reduction.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND TRACK
reviewVariables.text: Review pattern geometry and wind correction.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Review touchdown point against the 200-foot window.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards
source.taskName: Power-Off 180° Accuracy Approach and Landing (ASEL, ASES)

go-around.name: Go-Around / Rejected Landing
go-around.objective: Execute a go-around or rejected landing.

metrics.label: VX / VY
metrics.description: Transition to the appropriate climb speed.

metrics.label: VY to Safe Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain VY to a safe maneuvering altitude.

metrics.label: Climb
metrics.description: Establish a positive climb before configuration changes as appropriate.

criteria: Apply takeoff power immediately and establish the appropriate climb pitch.
Maintain VX or VY as appropriate within ±5 knots.
Retract flaps/gear in accordance with POH/AFM and a positive rate of climb.
Maintain directional control and wind correction.
Communicate as appropriate and complete checklist items.
Maintain VY within ±5 knots to a safe maneuvering altitude.

reviewVariables.label: DECISION
reviewVariables.text: Review timing of the go-around decision.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

steep-turns.name: Steep Turns

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Maintain approximately 50 degrees of bank within tolerance.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain entry altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain entry airspeed.

metrics.label: Rollout Heading
metrics.description: Roll out on the entry heading.

criteria: Clear the area and establish the specified entry airspeed and altitude.
Roll into a coordinated 360-degree turn with approximately 50 degrees of bank.
Maintain coordinated flight and appropriate division of attention.
Maintain entry altitude ±100 feet, airspeed ±10 knots, and bank ±5 degrees.
Complete the turn and roll out on the entry heading ±10 degrees.
Repeat in the opposite direction as required.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude control through the turn.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

steep-spiral.name: Steep Spiral
steep-spiral.objective: Perform a steep spiral around a selected ground reference.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Use bank as needed for wind while not exceeding 60 degrees.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the specified airspeed.

metrics.label: Rollout Heading
metrics.description: Roll out toward the selected object or specified heading.

criteria: Select a suitable ground reference and clear the area.
Establish and maintain a steep spiral with bank not exceeding 60 degrees.
Apply wind correction to maintain a constant radius around the selected reference.
Maintain coordinated flight and the specified airspeed within ±10 knots.
Complete the required turns while managing altitude and engine cooling as appropriate.
Roll out toward the selected object or specified heading within ±10 degrees.

reviewVariables.label: RADIUS
reviewVariables.text: Review ground-track radius around the reference.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

chandelle.name: Chandelle
chandelle.objective: Perform a chandelle with maximum performance and coordinated control.

metrics.label: Maximum Bank
metrics.description: Establish approximately 30 degrees of bank during the first 90 degrees of turn.

metrics.label: Rollout Heading
metrics.description: Complete rollout at the 180-degree point.

metrics.label: Final Airspeed
metrics.description: Finish at the minimum controllable airspeed appropriate to the maneuver, just above stall.

criteria: Clear the area and establish the recommended entry configuration, airspeed, and power.
Begin a coordinated climbing turn and establish approximately 30 degrees of bank.
During the first 90 degrees, increase pitch while maintaining bank.
During the second 90 degrees, hold pitch while smoothly decreasing bank.
Complete rollout at the 180-degree point within ±10 degrees.
Finish just above stall airspeed while maintaining coordinated flight.

reviewVariables.label: PITCH
reviewVariables.text: Review continuous pitch increase in the first half.

reviewVariables.label: ENERGY
reviewVariables.text: Review airspeed decay and power use.

reviewVariables.label: 180° POINT
reviewVariables.text: Review rollout heading and final airspeed.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

lazy-eights.name: Lazy Eights
lazy-eights.objective: Perform coordinated lazy eights with smooth continuously changing pitch and bank.

metrics.label: Maximum Bank
metrics.description: Reach approximately 30 degrees of bank at the steepest point.

metrics.label: Altitude at 180°
metrics.description: Return to entry altitude at each 180-degree point.

metrics.label: Airspeed at 180°
metrics.description: Return to entry airspeed at each 180-degree point.

metrics.label: Heading at 180°
metrics.description: Reach the planned 180-degree heading.

criteria: Clear the area and select suitable visual references.
Use smooth, continuous, coordinated changes in pitch and bank.
Reach the required pitch/bank relationships at the 45-, 90-, and 135-degree points.
Reach approximately 30 degrees of bank at the steepest point.
At each 180-degree point, return to entry altitude ±100 feet and airspeed ±10 knots.
Reach the planned heading at each 180-degree point within ±10 degrees.

reviewVariables.label: SMOOTHNESS
reviewVariables.text: Review continuity of pitch and bank changes.

reviewVariables.label: HEADING
reviewVariables.text: Review heading accuracy at each half-cycle.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

eights-on-pylons.name: Eights on Pylons
eights-on-pylons.objective: Perform eights on pylons using pivotal altitude and wind correction.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Use the correct bank angle for conditions, not exceeding 40 degrees.

metrics.label: Pivotal Altitude
metrics.description: Adjust altitude as required to keep the pylon visually stationary relative to the wing reference.

criteria: Select suitable pylons and an entry that accounts for wind.
Enter at the appropriate pivotal altitude and ground track.
Apply coordinated pitch and bank changes to keep each pylon on the selected visual reference.
Correct for wind while maintaining the appropriate pivotal relationship.
Use bank appropriate for conditions and not exceeding 40 degrees.
Transition smoothly between pylons while maintaining situational awareness and clearance.

reviewVariables.label: PYLON 1
reviewVariables.text: Review pivotal relationship around the first pylon.

reviewVariables.label: PYLON 2
reviewVariables.text: Review pivotal relationship around the second pylon.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review bank angle and wind correction.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

slow-flight.name: Maneuvering During Slow Flight
slow-flight.objective: Maneuver at slow speed while maintaining precise aircraft control.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain specified altitude.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain specified heading.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the specified slow-flight airspeed.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Maintain specified angle of bank.

criteria: Clear the area and establish the specified configuration.
Establish an airspeed that results in the required slow-flight condition without activating a stall warning.
Maintain coordinated flight while performing specified straight-and-level flight, turns, climbs, or descents.
Maintain altitude ±50 feet and heading ±10 degrees.
Maintain airspeed +5/-0 knots and specified bank ±5 degrees.
Recover to normal flight as directed while maintaining control.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review precision near the slow-flight target.

reviewVariables.label: RECOVERY
reviewVariables.text: Review transition back to normal flight.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

power-off-stall.name: Power-Off Stall
power-off-stall.objective: Demonstrate recognition and recovery from a power-off stall.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain specified heading if performed in straight flight.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: If turning, maintain specified bank not exceeding 20 degrees, within ±5 degrees.

metrics.label: Recovery
metrics.description: Recover at the first indication or after a full stall as specified by the evaluator.

criteria: Clear the area and select an altitude that permits safe completion.
Configure for the specified approach/landing condition and establish coordinated flight.
Transition smoothly to the pitch attitude that induces the stall.
Maintain specified heading ±10 degrees or specified bank not exceeding 20 degrees within ±5 degrees.
Recognize stall cues and recover as specified by the evaluator using appropriate procedures.
Configure for climb and return to the altitude, heading, and airspeed specified by the evaluator.

reviewVariables.label: ENTRY
reviewVariables.text: Review configuration and energy before stall entry.

reviewVariables.label: RECOVERY
reviewVariables.text: Review angle-of-attack reduction and power use.

reviewVariables.label: CLIMB
reviewVariables.text: Review return to normal climb configuration.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

power-on-stall.name: Power-On Stall
power-on-stall.objective: Demonstrate recognition and recovery from a power-on stall.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain specified heading if performed in straight flight.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: If turning, maintain specified bank not exceeding 20 degrees within ±10 degrees.

metrics.label: Power
metrics.description: Use no less than 65 percent power for the maneuver.

metrics.label: Recovery
metrics.description: Recover at the first indication or after a full stall as specified by the evaluator.

criteria: Clear the area and select an altitude that permits safe completion.
Establish the takeoff, departure, or cruise configuration specified by the evaluator.
Set power to no less than 65 percent.
Transition smoothly to the pitch attitude that induces the stall while maintaining coordinated flight.
Maintain specified heading ±10 degrees or turning-bank requirement until the stall occurs.
Recognize stall cues, recover as specified, configure for climb, and return to the evaluator-specified altitude, heading, and airspeed.

reviewVariables.label: POWER
reviewVariables.text: Review power setting and pitch entry.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

accelerated-stall.name: Accelerated Stall
accelerated-stall.objective: Demonstrate recognition and recovery from an accelerated stall.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Establish and maintain a coordinated turn in a 45-degree bank.

metrics.label: Entry Altitude
metrics.description: Select an entry altitude allowing completion no lower than 3,000 feet AGL.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Do not exceed maneuvering speed or other applicable POH/AFM limitation.

metrics.label: Recovery
metrics.description: Execute stall recovery using the aircraft procedure.

criteria: Clear the area and select an entry altitude allowing completion no lower than 3,000 feet AGL.
Establish the configuration specified by the evaluator and remain within applicable speed limitations.
Establish and maintain a coordinated 45-degree bank turn.
Increase elevator back pressure smoothly until an impending stall occurs.
Recognize the stall cues and execute the appropriate recovery.
Configure for climb and return to the altitude, heading, and airspeed specified by the evaluator.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

emergency-descent.name: Emergency Descent
emergency-descent.objective: Perform an emergency descent appropriate to the scenario and aircraft.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Use bank between 30 and 45 degrees to maintain positive load factors during descent.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the appropriate emergency-descent airspeed.

metrics.label: Level-Off Altitude
metrics.description: Level off at the specified altitude.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Use the configuration and procedures appropriate to the aircraft and scenario.

criteria: Clear the area and establish the airspeed/configuration appropriate to the scenario and POH/AFM.
Maintain orientation and divide attention appropriately.
Use 30 to 45 degrees of bank during the descent.
Maintain the appropriate airspeed +0/-10 knots.
Level off at the specified altitude within ±100 feet.
Complete appropriate checklist items and maintain situational awareness.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review speed against the emergency-descent target.

reviewVariables.label: ORIENTATION
reviewVariables.text: Review situational awareness and traffic/terrain considerations.

reviewVariables.label: RECOVERY
reviewVariables.text: Review smooth transition to level flight.

source.documentTitle: Commercial Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

emergency-approach-and-landing.name: Emergency Approach and Landing
emergency-approach-and-landing.objective: Plan and execute a simulated emergency approach and landing.

metrics.label: Best Glide
metrics.description: Establish and maintain the recommended best-glide airspeed.

metrics.label: Landing Area
metrics.description: Select a suitable landing area considering altitude, wind, terrain, obstructions, and glide distance.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Configure the airplane in accordance with POH/AFM and existing conditions.

criteria: Establish and maintain recommended best-glide airspeed within ±10 knots.
Configure the airplane in accordance with POH/AFM and existing conditions.
Select a suitable landing area considering altitude, wind, terrain, obstructions, and glide distance.
Plan and follow a flightpath to the selected landing area.
Prepare for landing as specified by the evaluator.
Complete appropriate emergency checklist items.

reviewVariables.label: BEST GLIDE
reviewVariables.text: Review capture and stability of best-glide speed.

reviewVariables.label: GLIDEPATH
reviewVariables.text: Review energy management to the selected area.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review wind effect on glide and pattern.

reviewVariables.label: CHECKLIST
reviewVariables.text: Review emergency checklist and task prioritization.
